title: Late-Night Drink Clustering
dataSources: Alcohol drinks (`alcohol:drink`), vice logs (`vice:log`), hydration intake (`hydration:intake`), swear-jar entries (`swearjar:entry`).
app: Habit and sobriety trackers, alcohol-unit and hydration logs, vaping/smoking cessation apps, and a smart swear jar — sent to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs and MQTT.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=alcohol:drink
| eval hour=tonumber(strftime(_time,"%H"))
| where hour>=21
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as late_drinks, sum(units) as units by _time
| sort - _time
description: Shows how much drinking is concentrated late at night rather than spread across social meals or events.
value: Late-night clustering often maps to lower-quality decisions, worse sleep, and habits that feel smaller than they are.
implementation: Ingest alcohol events with unit counts; report daily drinks and units taken after 9 PM.
visualization: Daily chart of late-night drinks and units.
grandmaExplanation: It spots how much of your drinking happens late at night, when habits tend to be less deliberate and more costly.
